title: Duplicate Authorization Control and Claim-Line Matching in Referrals and Authorizations
content:
Under **Referrals and Authorizations**, two authorizations of the same type for the same patient and the same servicing provider whose validity spans overlap are duplicates.

## 1. The duplicate rule

1. A new request that would duplicate an approved, unexpired authorization is denied as a duplicate request, and the patient is pointed to the authorization already on file.
2. A request for a different servicing provider, or for a different authorization type, is never a duplicate.
3. An approval requires that the request is not a duplicate of an approved authorization of the same type for the same patient and servicing provider whose validity span overlaps it. The check is made before the approval, on the system record of the patient's authorizations, not on the caller's account: the request is matched to the authorizations on file by patient, authorization type and servicing provider; only authorizations whose status is approved are compared; and the comparison is between the validity spans (first day and last day) of the two.

## 2. Which authorization a claim line uses

When several approved authorizations could cover one claim line, the line consumes the one whose servicing provider is the line's provider; among those, it consumes the one with the earliest last day of the validity span that still has units.

## 3. Judgement table

| Same type | Same patient | Same servicing provider | Spans overlap | Authorization on file approved | Duplicate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| no | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| yes | yes | no | yes | yes | no |

## 4. Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A patient holds an approved Specialty Care Referral to a network specialist whose span runs from 2 March to 28 August. A second Specialty Care Referral request to the same specialist with a span that would start on 1 June overlaps it and is denied as a duplicate request; the patient is pointed to the referral on file.
- The same patient asks for a Specialty Care Referral to a different specialist for the same months: a different servicing provider, so it is never a duplicate.
- Two approved authorizations of the patient both list the line's provider as servicing provider, one ending on 30 April with units left and one ending on 30 May: the claim line consumes the one ending on 30 April.
